source_name: Newgen (Newgen Software - NewgenONE low-code process automation / BPM platform and NewgenONE Marvin GenAI; newgensoft.com and landing.newgensoft.com)
enumeration_method: newgensoft.com plus its brochure host landing.newgensoft.com. Start: the site's own sitemap index (/sitemap.xml), which lists exactly 12 sub-sitemaps - category, csr-gallery, csr-initiatives, csr-programs, events, newsletter, p_platform, page, page_solutions, post, press-releases, recognition - holding 607 URLs. Those 12 do not cover the site: the union of every in-page link adds 193 further in-site routes (a whole /resources/ news, ebook, podcast and analyst-report section, 20 /platform/ pages, 34 /solutions/ pages, 22 /company/ pages, the /csr/ sections, blog posts, country-prefixed variants such as /au and /in, and demo/contact landings). The population is the union, 800 URLs; every one was fetched and every one returned HTTP 200. Closure was re-checked after the union: re-running the internal-link diff against the 800 leaves only asset URLs (/wp-content/...), share links and mailto/tel, none of which is a page. No keyword facet was used to narrow anything. The three landing.newgensoft.com brochure landing pages are counted as items and are public, so no BLOCKED row was needed. Note on TLS: newgensoft.com rejects Python's urllib with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED, so every fetch shelled out to curl, which validates the real chain; verification was never disabled.
note: 800/800 URLs fetched over HTTPS with curl at roughly one request per second; no login, captcha, paywall or rate limit anywhere, so no BLOCKED row. Evidence channels and how complete each is. (1) Downloadable process files - complete: zero .bpmn/.dmn/.vsdx/.bpmn20.xml links exist across the 800 pages and across the 304 PDF/Office documents hosted on landing.newgensoft.com. (2) BPMN 2.0 XML inside a page - complete: zero pages contain a bpmn:/bpmndi:/semantic: prefixed element. (3) A rendered modeller canvas - complete: zero pages carry bpmn-js markup (djs-element, djs-shape, djs-connection, data-element-id). (4) Preformatted diagram blocks - complete: zero <pre> elements with content on any page. (5) ASCII/box-drawing sketches - complete: zero body regions contain box-drawing characters (the 43 raw-page hits were mojibake inside one Arabic-named upload filename). (6) Body text naming BPMN - exactly one page of 800 mentions the string at all: /platform/process-automation/process-modeling/ ('Visually design simple to complex process models with both abstract and BPMN views'). (7) PDF text layer - 304 documents downloaded and converted with pdftotext; exactly one contains the string 'BPMN' (the NewgenOne Marvin brochure, where GenAI writes the model, i.e. design-time AI, not an AI element inside a process). (8) Figures, the weakest channel and the only one that is not complete. Every judgement was made on the page's own body region, taken between the last </header> and the first <footer>, because the site's mega-menu names 'NewgenONE Marvin GenAI' on all 800 pages and a whole-page keyword test would flag the entire population. Figures were handled in two passes. Channel A (all 800 pages): a figure whose file name or alt text names a process surface (bpmn, process, workflow, flowchart, orchestration, swimlane, gateway, designer, screen-shot, model, diagram) and which is not site furniture; 64 pages matched after removing the stock pictograms, whose own SVG markup identifies them (eight vendor icons carry the Font Awesome Pro 6.4.2 commercial-licence header or the SVG Repo upload header, and Advance-Processing-Rules.svg is 1447 bytes with four <path> elements and no text node). Channel B (the 34 pages whose own text discusses the process model itself): their figures were downloaded and measured - a drawn diagram or UI screenshot sits on a large flat near-white background and uses few colours, a photograph does not - and pages whose figures all measured photographic (13 of them) are excluded E0 on that measurement rather than on their file names. OPEN GAP, the only one in this census: a diagram whose file name AND alt text are both content-free, on a page that discusses only 'workflow' or 'process automation' rather than the process model itself, cannot be found by either pass. That broader set is 475 pages and 916 figures. Figures were not rendered in this session (the agent cannot read images), so every captured figure is verdict UNCERTAIN with needs_visual_check true and capture_quality null, and all 98 captures are listed in the corpus for the researcher's eye. No item was excluded for being marketing material, small, simple, non-English, fictional, low quality or similar to another item, and no figure was excluded for being one the agent could not see. Step 1 Use-Case Elicitation, Pass 2 per-source census. Verdicts are not the agent's to finalise: every UNCERTAIN row is a review task, and the ledger keeps every rejection so a false negative can be caught. VISUAL PASS (2026-09-25): image rendering became available and all 72 UNCERTAIN rows were opened and looked at, first as contact sheets then individually where a tile could not be read. Result: 2 rows are INCLUDE (rows 511 and 516: the NewgenONE Process Designer in BPMN View drawing a credit-card process with a service task labelled "AI Rule Engine" and the outgoing flow labelled "AI Decisioning" - a BPMN 2.0 model with an AI element inside the process); 1 row stays UNCERTAIN because the notation of the Process Insights process map could not be settled (row 515); 10 rows are E1-not-bpmn, each naming the notation it actually is (RPA script screen, ML pipeline node graph, Marvin design-time generation screen, layered architecture diagram, entity-relationship data model); 59 rows are E0-no-artefact, visually confirmed as social cards, stock photos, logos, banners or UI screens/forms/tables with no process model. The records and captures of the 69 rejected rows were moved to ledgers/newgen.raw/visual-check/ rather than deleted, and each rejected row names its file there in visual_evidence. No figure was excluded for being one the agent could not see. VISUAL BACKSTOP (2026-09-25): all 1117 broader-set figures (508 pages) were viewed on 94 contact sheets with a per-tile sidecar, as a check on the 800 recorded verdicts, because the DOM/text pass could not see image content. One figure carried a BPMN canvas the text pass had missed - row 513, now a record - and one claimed hit (row 517) was read at native size and rejected: that asset is the Process Management configuration table, as already recorded. Raster figures were judged from the sheet, every process-shaped or unreadable one re-read at full size. SVG assets cannot be rasterised by the sheet builder (PIL UnidentifiedImageError); all 261 of them were resolved instead by reading their markup - every one is a single-glyph or logo asset, none contains a <text> node, and a scan for bpmn/sequenceFlow/serviceTask tokens over the whole SVG set found only base64-embedded raster data. Figures that the sheet could not render therefore did not hide a diagram. Nothing in this pass was excluded for being unreadable: the one asset whose source resolution is too small to judge (row 500, admin-ajax.webp, 300x164) was read at native size and is a browser window with a tree panel and a list, not a process model. Near-misses seen and left as non-BPMN, for the researcher's awareness: the Data Science Studio ML-pipeline node graphs (rows 436, 443), the Content Intelligence data-flow diagram (row 446), the InsureMO layered-architecture diagram (row 484), the Section 1071 decision-tree infographic (row 688) and the Newgen Health capability map whose top strip reads 'Payer Operations BPaaS Automation with AI/ML/RPA' (rows 111, 020) - an AI-labelled element inside a capability map, not inside a process.
